newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Milling wheat up in trendless Budapest mkt.
newsitem.headline: Milling wheat up in trendless Budapest mkt.

text.p: Most milling wheat futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) rose on Friday due to a technical correction in an otherwise trendless market, dealers said.
"The rise was mainly an (upward) correction of too small spreads," said Robert Vajo of Termin, adding that deferred maturities were relatively undervalued compared with the nearest one, August.
August milling wheat eased 70 forints per tonne to 20,480 while all other wheat maturities rose, by between 40 and 230 forints.
Vajo added that the market was trendless and that it could move either way in the coming days.

"When harvesting starts, that could depress (wheat) prices," he said. "On the other hand, some traders who look at international trends, expect an upward correction as wheat prices dropped some $50 per tonne over the last two months".
Total grains turnover plummeted to 437 lots or 187.8 million forints from Thursday's 1,709 lots or 736.4 million forints.
Milling wheat accounted for the bulk of the turnover in volume terms with almost 300 lots.
